churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, types and configuration are each behind one well-defined seam, so API and requirement changes are localized. Docked for the loosened (non-CLI-default) template type-checking, scroll logic spread across three components, and the server duplicating the route list.

findings.issue: resource() loaders never forward the loader's abortSignal to fetch, so changing params (typing in search, switching game, navigating away) leaves stale requests running; the Angular resource guide says to always pass abortSignal to fetch
findings.suggestion: Thread the loader's abortSignal through PokeApi.get (e.g. an optional signal argument that also clears the in-flight cache entry on abort)

findings.issue: strictTemplates (and the CLI's other strict angularCompilerOptions) omitted, so template type errors are silent — the $any($event.target) cast in home.html:18 is a direct symptom; a current ng new generates these flags
findings.suggestion: Set strictTemplates: true (and ideally strictDomEventTypes/strictAttributeTypes) and remove the $any cast with a typed event handler

findings.issue: @angular/forms is a declared dependency but is never imported by any source file
findings.suggestion: Remove it, or, if it stays, use Signal Forms (stable in v22) for the home filters — its debounce() rule would replace the hand-rolled search debounce

findings.issue: Scroll restoration is hand-rolled here and again in home.ts:64-68 and pokemon-page.ts:63-66, duplicating router scroll behavior that withInMemoryScrolling (stable) or v22's withExperimentalPlatformNavigation already provides
findings.suggestion: Consolidate into one scroll service (or router scroll options), keeping only the one piece that genuinely needs custom logic — jumping to #moves after async data arrives

findings.issue: The search debounce plus lastSearchSent echo-guard is imperative, mutable-field bookkeeping where Signal Forms' debounce() rule or linkedSignal expresses the same 'state follows the URL unless locally edited' declaratively
findings.suggestion: Model searchText as linkedSignal({source: q input}) or a Signal Forms field with debounce(200), deleting the timer bookkeeping and the DestroyRef cleanup

findings.issue: The server keeps a second copy of the app's route knowledge (DETAIL_ROUTES/STATIC_ROUTES) to decide 404 status; a new page needs matching edits in both server.mjs and app.routes.ts
findings.suggestion: Derive the route list from one shared module (imported by both), or drop the API 404 probe and let the app handle not-found, which the spec makes optional

findings.issue: Recursive evolution tree via *ngTemplateOutlet is the app's only pre-control-flow idiom; it works but is the style a v17-era codebase used
findings.suggestion: Extract a small recursive EvolutionList component (or use a data-driven depth nesting) so the modern component-only pattern is uniform

findings.issue: Two title mechanisms coexist: syncPageTitle effects for data-driven pages and static route titles in app.routes.ts:8,10 — future title rules (e.g. a new suffix) must be changed in both
findings.suggestion: Register a custom TitleStrategy with the router and have data-driven pages expose their heading through it

findings.issue: The cache Map only deletes entries on error; expired entries keep their resolved payloads in memory for the life of the app (bounded by the API's size, so acceptable, but it grows over a long session)
findings.suggestion: Sweep expired entries (cheap on get, or a periodic prune) so the TTL actually reclaims memory

summary: This is a genuinely current Angular v22 codebase — @Service, resource, signal inputs, @let, zoneless and OnPush-by-default — with a clean single-module data boundary, runtime-injected API config, and a lean platform-first implementation (fetch, URL, AbortSignal.timeout, native form controls, CSS custom properties). The gaps are small but real: the resource abortSignal is never passed to fetch, strictTemplates was dropped from the CLI's strict defaults (hence $any in a template), @angular/forms is declared but unused, and a few behaviors (search debounce, scroll restoration, recursive template) are hand-rolled where current primitives exist. I'd merge after the abortSignal and strictTemplates fixes; the rest are follow-up hygiene items that won't age the code badly.
